$note: Source-of-truth values for brand tokens, mirrored by hand into apps/web/src/app/globals.css (CSS custom properties) and, later, a Flutter theme file. No build pipeline generates either target yet — until one exists, keep both in sync manually when you change a value here. Palette is OmniSift's frozen brand identity (warm cream/ivory + dark chocolate brown + gold) — refine, never replace with a blue/purple theme.

color.accentDark$note: Corrected from the original #C98F26 (2.1:1 on white — fails WCAG's 3:1 non-text-contrast minimum) — both apps.web (--color-accent-dark) and apps.client (AppColors.accentDark) already independently applied this exact fix; this file was the one that hadn't been updated to match. Use for anything that must actually be seen clearly (icons, star ratings, text), not accent itself.
color.successDanger$note: apps/web darkens these for WCAG AA text contrast (success #18773f, danger #b82d28 — see globals.css) and apps/client uses its own distinct pair again (success #2E9E4B, error #E5484D — see AppColors). All three are real, already-shipped, deliberate values, not a bug in any one of them — recorded here rather than picking a 'correct' one and silently overwriting a shipped app's colors.

semantic.$note: How the raw `color.*` palette above maps to each platform's actual semantic roles (P1 design-token reconciliation pass). This file documents the vocabulary; it isn't consumed programmatically by either app yet (see the top-level $note).

brand.primary.web: color.brand (#3B2314) — used directly for primary text/CTAs on the warm cream surface.
brand.primary.client: AppColors.primary (#4A2C17) + AppColors.primaryLight (#6B4429) + AppColors.secondary (#B25D3A, warm terracotta) — a distinct, wider set of brand roles for the app shell (buttons, nav, chips), not a 1:1 reuse of color.brand. Same warm family, chosen independently for Flutter's UI density.

surface.*.web: color.background / color.backgroundSubtle / color.cream / color.beige — the warm cream→beige neutral ramp used for page/card backgrounds.
surface.*.client: AppColors.background (#FAFAFA) / AppColors.surface (#FFFFFF) / AppColors.border (#E0E0E0) — a separate, cooler light-grey neutral scale for the app shell's cards/surfaces, deliberately distinct from web's warm ramp (the app UI reads as a cleaner, denser surface than the editorial web pages; not a drift to fix).

text.*.web: color.ink (#2B1B12) for primary text, color.muted (#7A6A5C) for secondary/caption text.
text.*.client: AppColors.textPrimary (#1A1A1A), AppColors.textSecondary (#666666), AppColors.textDisabled (#707070, darkened from #9E9E9E for WCAG AA — also used for real muted content, not just disabled controls). No equivalent tokens existed in this file before this pass.

chart.series.$note: Explicit brand-palette EXCEPTION, not an oversight — product-owner decision (earlier session): chart series need to be visually distinguishable from each other and from the warm brand palette (which would make multi-line price-history charts hard to read), so this palette is deliberately NOT warm-toned.
chart.series.client: apps/client/lib/features/products/presentation/screens/price_graph_screen.dart's _seriesColors — the only place these are used.

logo.iconOnly: logo-mark-light.svg / logo-mark-dark.svg — compact placements (nav headers, favicons)
logo.fullLockup: logo-full.png (icon + cursive wordmark + tagline, transparent background) — footer, splash, marketing/hero placements. Source master at logo-full-transparent.png; logo-full.png here is the original opaque-background file as provided.
